name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa; Sudan, South Sudan and Yemen hard hit
state: WHO said around 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people have died of cholera in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa, after nearly 7,900 deaths in 2025, the deadliest year since 1999; Sudan, South Sudan, DR Congo, Nigeria and Yemen are among the worst-affected countries (SCMP; The Standard, citing AFP). In Europe, ECDC counted 76 locally acquired dengue cases in Italy and 8 in France by 11 Nov, with none new in the latest week (ECDC). Searches on 18 Nov found no sign of the cholera toll easing, so high mortality in conflict zones keeps the Alert.
for_you: Travellers to affected areas can check NHS fit for travel and FCDO travel advice for cholera and dengue precautions. Risk in the UK is very low.
rubric_hit: Alert: large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (WHO: over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026; Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen)

sources.title: SCMP — Over 3,000 already dead from cholera this year, says WHO

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
